pr_title: Add button to override duplicate hotkeys
pr_body:
1. Add a button to override duplicate hotkeys (the button is the size of the "Logout" button and is not visible if there are no duplicates).
1. Make the <kbd>Esc</kbd> key cancel an active rebind (to give the user a way out of the focused state).

![override-common](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1355810/74184984-71e2b900-4c50-11ea-8e74-3c299effa7bc.png)

Closes #17599
pr_comments: I'm a bit hesitant about having the override button inside the text field and the others outside - this doesn't feel consistent. Have you considered other ways which we could present this?
@pchote I am also a bit hesitant because of the inconsistency. I considered some alternatives, see #17599 for mock-ups and earlier tests I had made.

What if we keep the same behaviour as the current PR, but instead of displaying it inset in the text field, we make the text field narrower and show the override button with the same size/style as the clear and reset buttons (which would not move or change)?

> What if we keep the same behaviour as the current PR, but instead of displaying it inset in the text field, we make the text field narrower and show the override button with the same size/style as the clear and reset buttons (which would not move or change)?

Do you mean like this:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1355810/83353629-86140880-a35c-11ea-99ee-76dbd40d1bf5.png)

I tried that, the problem is that field becomes too narrow for bindings with more than one modifier (see https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/issues/17599#issuecomment-580413428).

yeah, but only when there is a conflict. Otherwise, it would look the same as now with the wider field and two buttons.

IMO the narrow field should be fine, because this will already be a rare occurrence, and we have a tooltip to show the full binding when hovering (right?)

@pchote Like this?

![hotkey-override](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1355810/83676645-b02b2c00-a5e3-11ea-974a-d175bb8b25c3.gif)

How to change the width of the input with only yaml? Once yoga is in the reflow will be automatic I guess. 

And the hotkey widget doesn't support tooltips.

Yeah exactly like that. It can be implemented by subtracting (clear button X - override button X) from the text field width and unhiding the override button in the logic handler when the conflict is detected.
> And the hotkey widget doesn't support tooltips. We have it for the main list but I see that we may indeed not for the entry field - we should fix that to match.

Update: changed the button to look like https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/pull/17666#issuecomment-638398417

@pchote Adding tool tip support to `HotkeyEntryWidget` seems a bit like a can of worms. Could we do that in a follow-up?
Update: just a force push because the Travis build was stuck.
Leaving tooltips to a followup is fine by me.

issue_context.title: Improve usability when remaping duplicate hotkeys
issue_context.body:
## Motivation
<!-- Please provide a clear and concise description of the motivation behind the request. If your request is related to a problem or limitation, describe it below. -->

Recently I played the game on a new PC and since I use a highly customized hotkey layout I had to remap a lot of keys. However that proved to be quite cumbersome because if I the key I'm trying to remap is already bound to something else I'd first have to go to that other binding and change it. So it becomes a multi-step back and forth process:

1. Try to remap X
1. Receive warning that this key is already mapped to Y
1. Find Y
1. Remap Y (or clear it)
1. Go back to X and complete intended the remap

## Proposed solution
<!-- Please describe your idea and how it is intended to address the motivation of your request. Provide a clear and concise description of the proposed changes. -->

I suggest we add a way to override the duplicate during the initial remap. This would make the process much easier because it would eliminate the back and forth to remap the other key. 

1. Try to remap X
1. Receive warning that this keys is already mapped to Y
1. Override Y

I came up with two ways to represent this in the dialog:

### Additional "Assign / Override" button

![hotkey-override--button](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1355810/72810578-8b529f80-3c66-11ea-8be1-65ed73a34a92.png)

This button would be always visible but only become active when there is a duplicate. The downside is that in most cases this button would not serve any purpose.

This can be worked-around by having the button appear inside the input field only when necessary:

![hotkey-override--inline](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1355810/72988652-56288780-3df5-11ea-86d9-1126b3a9fba4.png)


### An overlay dialog

![hotkey-override--dialog](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1355810/72810717-cce34a80-3c66-11ea-9c86-5e5a7235267a.png)

This works around the need to have a third button. The downside is that it obscures the original dialog and we'd have to repeat everything to make ourselves clear (hotkey description, desired key combo, duplicate hotkey description).
comments:
A working prototype: 
![изображение](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1355810/73102554-c1a84d00-3efa-11ea-98c9-0440d3b5ca87.png)

Perhaps the button looks a little off

> This button would be always visible but only become active when there is a duplicate. The downside is that in most cases this button would not serve any purpose.

We could always show the assign button and require the user to press it to set a hotkey. The text could then change to "override" in case of a conflict. (I hope that will make immediately clear to the user what is going on and what the override button is going to do, i.e. "aha, instead of assigning I need to override this key".)

> 
> 
> > This button would be always visible but only become active when there is a duplicate. The downside is that in most cases this button would not serve any purpose.
> 
> We could always show the assign button and require the user to press it to set a hotkey. The text could then change to "override" in case of a conflict. (I hope that will make immediately clear to the user what is going on and what the override button is going to do, i.e. "aha, instead of assigning I need to override this key".)

Yes, that's an option too. I thought about it but forgot to mention it in the OP. The downside is that it adds a step to the rebinding process (user always has to press "Assign" instead of the game auto-assigning a valid key). 

When a key is in this limbo state a "Cancel" button also makes sense - if the user realizes they don't want to assign/override a key. The way out now is to click on another key or navigate away from the hotkeys tab.

I don't think an extra action is a problem here while explicit assigning is an improvement. (The user now knows for sure they set the key. Before they were left wondering if they needed to press enter, or if leaving the field cancelled, etc.) Fwiw, if I was to just change a single hotkey and didn't know the code, I would not immediately use the back button to leave but make sure the game actually set the hotkey by switching to another key and back.

As you said, a cancel button would be useful for similar reasons. If we already have assign then cancel might be superfluous however.
It might also get very crowded with two more buttons, so we could use your overlay idea and always show the overlay once a key is pressed? (I'm not yet completely sold on that.)

I have prototyped both approaches (1) explicit "Assign" button and (2) auto-assign with "Override" when needed) and I think that auto-assign works better. I find it more fluid and easier to use - there are less steps needed for a rebind and it also falls in line with the approach OpenRA has taken for other settings - they instantly apply. With an "Assign" button an extra step is required of the user, even when using the "Reset" button on a hotkey (as there may be duplicates).

However we're running out of space in the dialog when the "Override" button is visible all the time:
![override-hotkey](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1355810/73481933-72a06300-43a5-11ea-87d4-f511a2c5b51b.png)

Perhaps we should put the description on its own line (like in earlier prototypes of the dialog):
![изображение](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1355810/73482505-8c8e7580-43a6-11ea-9493-4d90eb7d6b76.png)

review_comments: Moving these here will change `HandleKeyPress` to return false and not call `YieldKeyboardFocus`. Have you considered the implications for this?

The only time when the user can press <kbd>Enter</kbd> is when the hotkey is invalid. And since losing focus triggers hotkey validation the field just goes back to the focused state. That's why I added the return/enter keys to the list of ignored keys - to spare that round-trip through the logic. 

I thought about wiring <kbd>Enter</kbd> to the override action since that key is usually used to accept things (and is the opposite of <kbd>Esc</kbd>). But perhaps it isn't too obvious in this case that pressing enter would result in an override and it may be an unexpected action.
Ah, my bad. I somehow missed that this was `HotkeyEntryWidget` and not the more general `TextFieldWidget`.
A small followup PR will be able to use this to unfocus the lobby chat and fix #15426.
